newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Aussie Home complains to ACCC about CBA ads.
newsitem.headline: Aussie Home complains to ACCC about CBA ads.

text.p: Mortgage originator Aussie Home Loans said on Monday it had lodged a complaint with the Australian Competition and Consumer Commission (ACCC) about an advertising campaign by Commonwealth Bank of Australia.
The bank recently advertised its "economiser" mortgage rate of 6.35 percent as being a lower rate than offered by Aussie.

"The Commonwealth Bank is totally misrepresenting its own no-frills, basic 'economiser' rate of 6.35 percent by stating in radio, TV and press ads that it has a lower variable rate than Aussie Home Loans," Symond said in a statement.

However, Commonweath Bank's general manager personal banking, Alf Long, said the bank's variable rate below that offered by Aussie Home Loans and had a lower establishment fee as well as a number of other features.
"The Commonwealth Bank's advertising is dead accurate," Long said in a statement. "Aussie Home loans would do better to stop bleating and start competing," he said.
Symond said the comparison between the Aussie rate and Commonwealth Bank's rate was invalid. "The Commonwealth Bank is not comparing apples with apples," he said.
